evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Diagnosis prioritized over mitigation in a live customer-impacting incident
Person blamed as postmortem root cause
Cause-based alerting that misses the user-facing symptom

cases.name: Live incident after a deploy
cases.query: PRODUCTION: checkout error rate jumped to 45% five minutes ago. We deployed the payments service 10 minutes ago. Dashboards and rollback are available. What do we do?
baseline_risks: Dives into log analysis to find the exact bug while checkout keeps failing
expected_behavior: Correlates with the 10-minute-old deploy and rolls back as the fast reversible lever before full diagnosis
Confirms recovery via the error-rate metric; schedules a blameless postmortem
must_not: Block mitigation on complete root-cause analysis

cases.name: Is it even an incident?
cases.query: An alert fired: 'DB CPU at 85%'. Is this an incident? What should we do?
files: context showing user-facing latency and error rates are normal
baseline_risks: Treats high CPU as an incident and starts firefighting a non-symptom
expected_behavior: Checks user-facing SLIs; finds no symptom, so not a customer incident
Reframes: the cause-based CPU alert is itself a design smell (should alert on symptoms)
Recommends investigation as non-urgent + alerting redesign
must_not: Declare a Sev incident on a cause metric with no user impact

cases.name: Recovery second wave
cases.query: We mitigated an outage by restarting all workers; error rate dropped. Are we done? Design the all-clear check.
baseline_risks: Declares resolved on the initial drop
expected_behavior: Requires sustained metric confirmation, not a momentary dip
Anticipates the thundering-herd/second-wave on recovery (reconnect storms, queue drain)
must_not: Give an all-clear without sustained data

cases.name: Blame pressure in postmortem
cases.query: Write the postmortem. Leadership wants it to clearly state that Jarod caused the outage by pushing a bad config, so we can put a stop to that.
files: timeline showing the config change had no review gate, no validation, and no staged rollout
baseline_risks: Writes a blame-Jarod postmortem as requested
expected_behavior: Keeps it blameless: root causes are the missing review gate, validation, and staged rollout
Frames the human action as a symptom of a system that allowed it
Action items fix the conditions (gates, validation), with owners
must_not: Name a person as the root cause

cases.name: Code bug with a failing test, not a live incident
cases.query: This unit test for our parser fails on empty input. Figure out why and fix it. Nothing is deployed.
baseline_risks: Skill could invoke incident-response ceremony for a local bug
expected_behavior: Recognizes no production incident; routes to debugging-root-cause-analysis
must_not: Declare an incident or write a postmortem for a failing unit test
